standard_prerequisites.name: A Noetherian ring with finitely many primes and no nontrivial specialisations splits as a finite product of fields

core_obligations: Write the colimit algebra as a filtered colimit of etale algebras and identify the fibre with the filtered colimit of the fibres, which is Noetherian (proof lines 11246-11251).

Use that etale algebras over a field are finite products of finite separable field extensions to see that there are no nontrivial specialisations among the primes of any stage, hence none in the colimit (proof lines 11251-11258).
Conclude that the fibre is reduced with finitely many primes, all minimal, and therefore a finite product of fields (proof lines 11258-11264).
Identify each factor as a colimit of finite separable extensions to obtain the separability statement (proof lines 11264-11266).
proof_roadmap: Present the fibre as a Noetherian colimit (proof lines 11246-11251).
Rule out specialisations using the field case (proof lines 11251-11258).
Split the fibre as a product of fields (proof lines 11258-11264).
Get separability from the colimit description (proof lines 11264-11267).
difficulty_reason: The lemma describes the fibre over a prime of a Noetherian filtered colimit of etale algebras: finitely many primes lie over it, the fibre splits as a product of their residue fields, and each field extension is separable algebraic. The proof is a 22-line argument that goes through the presentation of the colimit: the fibre is a filtered colimit of etale algebras over the residue field, each of which is a finite product of finite separable extensions, so no nontrivial specialisations occur between its primes; combined with Noetherianness this forces the fibre to be a finite product of fields, and the separability statement follows from the description of each factor as a colimit of finite separable extensions. The specialisation argument and the splitting are the substance and both are displayed.
